questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'What Is a Civilisation?' refers to.
questions.a: A civilisation is an advanced stage of human society marked by government and administration, urbanism with town planning and cities, and shared systems such as writing, trade and technology.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'What Is a Civilisation?'.
questions.a: A civilisation is more than villages: it is society grown complex, with cities, officials and records.

questions.q: Under which section is 'What Is a Civilisation?' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: What is a civilisation (source: fees106.txt, What is a civilisation)

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'The Harappan Civilisation' refers to.
questions.a: The most ancient civilisation of the Indian subcontinent is known as the Harappan, Indus or Indus-Sarasvati Civilisation; it flourished along the Indus and the Sarasvati's course over four thousand years ago.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'The Harappan Civilisation'.
questions.a: One civilisation, three names: Harappan from the first site, Indus and Indus-Sarasvati from its rivers.

questions.q: Under which section is 'The Harappan Civilisation' taught, and from which source text?
Explain in your own words what 'Harappan Towns: Planning and Achievements' refers to.
questions.a: Harappan cities show careful town planning with grid streets, covered drains, fortified areas like Dholavira's castle, standardized bricks and weights, seals and bead work, and trade reaching distant lands.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Harappan Towns: Planning and Achievements'.
questions.a: Streets, drains and standard weights reveal a government that planned and a people that followed rules together.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Harappan Towns: Planning and Achievements' taught, and from which source text?
Explain in your own words what 'Harappan Society: Decline and Legacy' refers to.
questions.a: Harappan society was balanced rather than exploitative, with no glaring gulf between rich and poor; around 1900 BCE the cities declined, yet their farming, crafts, and town ways passed into later Indian life.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Harappan Society: Decline and Legacy'.
questions.a: What survives a civilisation's fall is its legacy: the Harappan ways quietly seeded the culture that followed.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Harappan Society: Decline and Legacy' taught, and from which source text?
